He is the elected ruler of Redridge Mountains. He is dedicated to keeping the town safe from orcs and gnolls. The dwarves of Ironforge sent a group to Lakeshire's aid, made up of Princess Moira Bronzebezard and her retinue, but they were ambushed and captured in the Burning Steppes. Many Redridge Citizens are currently lined up for an audience with the magistrate, angry with his inability to deal with the disappearances plaguing Lakeshire. The Magisters are a prominent group of blood elf mages and are one of three major factions in the government of Quel'Thalas, along with the Farstriders and the Blood Knights. They are led by the Grand Magister of Quel'Thalas, Rommath, a powerful archmage who succeeded Grand Magister Belo'vir after the Scourge invasion. They are a politically powerful group, its leaders having strong historic ties to the upper echelons of Silvermoon.

The Magic Broom is a temporary mount/item obtained from a quest, boss, or vendor during the Hallow's End seasonal event. It is instant cast and will adjust its speed and flight capability according to a character's riding skill, but can only be used during Hallow's End.
Magmaw's Fissure is an area within Blackwing Descent, where Magmaw is being held. The gaping hole, likely caused by Magmaw, reveals more of the under mountain city, Shadowforge City.

Magic breakers (also known as breakers) are a mysterious type of ogre immune to specific or all types of magic. They are found almost exclusively in the Chamber of Nullification of Highmaul. There are several categories such as felbreakers and firebreakers, each being able to actively dampen or nullify their affiliated magic.
Magical Affinity is a passive racial ability for all nightborne, increasing magical damage dealt.

Makers' Overlook is a titan facility located far above the ground in the eastern area of the Sholazar Basin. It is a titan-made building that seems to simply sprout from the sheer heights of the mountains on Sholazar's northeast side. The grand entrance leads to halls cut deep into the mountains, from which you can see rune-inscribed gears the size of a keep turning slowly in a massive machine. There's no knowing what the machine itself does. The Overlook, which can only be reached by flying, serves as a good vantage for observing the basin below. The titans constructed this vantage point where they oversaw their creations. Inside, particularly in the presence of the deep clockwork gears, it

Manaforge Duro is one of the five facilities that "collect" the chaotic magic of the Twisting Nether from the air of Netherstorm for Kael'thas' blood elves. It is being used near full capacity, and mana creatures are leaking out of the pipes as a result. Manaforge Duro is also the home of Summoner Kanthin, one of the most senior magisters of Prince Kael'thas. Duro is located on the floating island directly west of Tempest Keep.

Mana Tap was a blood elf racial ability used in combination with Arcane Torrent. This ability was removed in patch 3.0.2, partly due to lore reasons. In the closing hours of Burning Crusade the Sunwell was reignited and began to feed the sin'dorei addiction for magic again, thus removing the need to tap mana from other creatures. The practical reason however was that while it had its uses, such as a ranged cornerpulling tool for blood elf paladins, the mechanic to maintain three charges to release arcane torrent was deemed too much of a hassle, especially in raids and other content that required more attention to other functions. It is still referenced in the flirt emotes done by female bloo

.]] Mana rays (also known as skyfin) are flying creatures native to Argus. Skyfin can fly from birth and there are some observed cases of mothers giving birth midflight. They can be observed in a wide variety of colors. Biologists believe the vibrancy of those colors both help attract mates and ward predators.

Margaux is a nightborne vintner in charge of the running of the Twilight Vineyards in Suramar City. In her managerial role, she is responsible for the day-to-day upkeep of the vineyards, ensuring that they continue to produce the Arcwine which Suramar depends upon. Recently, however, with the instability that has engulfed the city, Margaux's task has become significantly more difficult.
__NOTOC__ Mariner Moonblade was a member of the Feathermoon Ferry, the boat that runs between Feathermoon Stronghold and The Forgotten Coast.

A city somewhere on Azeroth. This city was laid out by meticulous architects. Regrettably its wide streets and simple elegance attracted the attention of a passing warlord, whose army invaded the city shortly after.

Master's Call is a level 28 Cunning hunter pet ability. It removes and temporarily prevents movement impairing effects on the pet and a friendly target. When using Command Pet to cast this ability, if the selected target isn't friendly or if no target is selected, it will automatically target the hunter. This ability is available to all hunter specs as long as their current pet is a Cunning pet.

Master of Ghouls is a an Unholy death knight talent that allows your Ghoul to function like a regular pet instead of your guardian, enabling the simple pet commands Attack, Follow, Move To, Stay, the pet stances Aggressive, Defensive, and Passive, and ghoul-specific abilities Claw (ghoul ability), Gnaw (ghoul ability), Huddle and Leap. For more information, see Risen Ally.

Mathel's Flying Machine is a flying machine owned by Mathel Rustwrench. Mathel makes the vehicle available for chartered flights from the Gol'Bolar Quarry to the Ironforge Airfield. Player characters gain access to it for the quest Get to the Airfield.

Maztha is a flying trainer located in the Orgrimmar Skyway. She grants you Flight Master's License at a cost of , which allows you to ride flying mounts in the Eastern Kingdoms and Kalimdor. She is located in Loamm in Zaralek Cavern with other members of the Riders of Azeroth.

Mayla Highmountain is the High Chieftain of the Highmountain tauren and leader of the Highmountain Tribe, assuming the chieftainship after her father Ulan was killed by Dargrul at the beginning of the war against the Burning Legion. After Dargrul was slain and the Legion defeated, Mayla and her people joined their distant kin in Mulgore as members of the Horde. She became a staunch supporter of Baine Bloodhoof, speaking out in disgust when he was imprisoned for working against Sylvanas Windrunner's increasingly immoral actions during the Fourth War. She accompanied Baine during his meeting with Anduin Wrynn just prior to the return of N'Zoth, and was ultimately seated on the Horde Council as

Meditation is a passive ability that allows mana regeneration from Spirit to continue while in combat. It is gained automatically by choosing or switching to a healing specialization ie Restoration for druids, Discipline or Holy for priests and Restoration for shaman. The equivalent Mistweaver monk ability is functionally the same, but named Mana Meditation.

Med'an is a founder of the New Council of Tirisfal and a former wielder of Atiesh, Greatstaff of the Guardian. As the son of the human Medivh and the half-orc, half-draenei Garona Halforcen, Med'an is half-human, quarter-draenei, and quarter-orc. His unusual parentage and training has given him the unique ability to interweave shamanic magic with the arcane and divine. This gift, however, has also drawn him into conflict with cultists of the Twilight's Hammer who believed he was the subject of an ancient prophecy and dark entities who would make his power their own. Mechanolift 304 - A is a mechanical device found flying in a set path throughout the Iron Concourse in Ulduar. They can be destroyed with the siege vehicles' anti-air rockets. Once destroyed they drop Liquid Pyrite containers, which can be used by the Salvaged Demolishers. During the Fourth War, one was in the Inventor's Library in the Storm Peaks, being worked on by SCRAP-E.

Merithra, known as Merithra of the Dream, is the current Aspect of the green dragonflight and a child of the former Dragon Aspect Ysera. Following her mother's death, she became the de facto leader of the green dragonflight, until her ascension to Aspect on the Dragon Isles. During the War of the Ancients, Merithra led the green flight in the Ohn'ahran Plains of the Dragon Isles and forged a pact with Teera, the matriarch of the centaur clans. Millennia later, Merithra played a major role in the War of the Shifting Sands, but was taken captive by the qiraji and trapped in Ahn'Qiraj alongside the red Caelestrasz and the blue Arygos. Mental Recovery is a conduit for monks. It drops from Shriekwing in Castle Nathria, Zo'phex in Tazavesh, the Veiled Market, and the Lords of Dread in the Sepulcher of the First Ones. An ilvl 145 version is also rewarded from Strengthen the Bond, A Journey Made Together, Strengthening the Bond (Night Fae), and Strengthening the Bond (Venthyr).

Michael Garrett is a Forsaken flight master located in the Trade Quarter in the Undercity. Following the Battle for Lordaeron, he is located on the Gates of Orgrimmar in Orgrimmar alongside Wounded Forsaken Bats. Following the Forsaken reclaiming the Ruins of Lordaeron, Garrett and his bats returned to the city. He can be seen tending to the wounded ones.

Micro dungeon maps are maps added in Mists of Pandaria for micro dungeons that take place in the open world and not in a separate instance. Such micro dungeons include Blackrock Mountain (and not the instances it contains), the Caverns of Time, and the Gold Coast Quarry. Micro dungeon maps are organized based on what continent they appear in. A list of every mapped micro dungeon appears below organized alphabetically, regardless of continent. Follow the link to be taken directly to that area's map.

Mist-shaman are a type of yaungol shaman of the Osul tribe who use their magic to enslave the mistlurkers of the Townlong Steppes. Until recently, the mist-shaman would travel to the Sumprushes to work alongside the mistlurkers, but now they instead use their magic to enslave the creatures. A mist-shaman's magic flows through his torch, which is used as both totem and spell focus. The mist-shaman once used these torches to commune with the elementals, but now use them to break the creatures to the yaungol's will.

Molten giants, also known as magma giants or magma destroyers, are enormous fire elementals that resemble titan-forged mountain giants. They are native to the Firelands, but some have been pulled into Azeroth by . Though ultimately loyal to Ragnaros, the giants are kept in line by the heavy-handed rule of . These elementals are powerful, unpredictable and violent. The summoning and controlling of molten giants is forbidden by the Earthen Ring, as the use of such coercion could anger the elements and trigger an event similar to the Cataclysm. However, during the attack on Theramore Isle, ordered his dark shaman to force molten giants into battle.

The Molten Span is located inside Blackrock Mountain. It is the large central chamber with lava in the bottom and a central rock chained to the sides, containing Forgewright's Tomb. The Ironmarch took control of the upper Blackrock Spire within the mountain and dug a passage from the Spire Throne to the Molten Span. They erected a platform where they intended to prime one of their Iron stars which could act as a weapon of mass destruction capable of erupting an entire volcano. One of the buildings on the perimeter is the Stone Sentinel's Overlook, though the geometry from each side does not match.

The mogu empire (or Mogu Dynasty) possessed immense size and strength. The mogu built it based on might, in which the weak — other races — were subjugated, and the strong — always mogu — ascended to power. So brutal was their regime that its name is never uttered aloud: pandaren call it either the "Old Kingdom" or "First Dynasty". The mogu empire was a meritocracy, where the previous regime and/or dynasty must be overpowered and executed. The mogu empire was founded by Lei Shen, "The Thunder King." He united the mogu, defeated the other pandaren races, and built an empire that would last for thousands of years.

Molten Cay is an Island Expedition in Battle for Azeroth. It is a tropical island with a volcano and Zandalari ruins. The island is inhabited by ogres, yaungol, and sand and jungle trolls. Gorlocs, saurok and tol'vir can also be found here, including obsidian black dragonkin.

The Mooncloth set is not a true set because it does not provide set bonuses. The individual pieces provide bonuses to Intellect, Spirit, and Stamina. This is set is attractive to Warlocks, Mages, and possibly Priests because of the stat bonuses. This set primarily focuses on the HP and Mana pools of the caster. Like the Cindercloth set, this set has 2 chest pieces: a vest and a robe. Stat bonuses for each combination are shown below. The pattern for the Mooncloth Robe is found in Dire Maul. The pattern for the Mooncloth Boots is a quest reward requiring friendly reputation with Timbermaw Hold.
An island somewhere on Azeroth. Ogres and trolls hold most of this islands riches, but golems maintain a sleepless vigil over the island's center.

Moon Horror Den is a small cave inhabited by Raging Owlbeasts. However, they may not always be there, as many players complete Wild Guardians. It is situated quite close to Everlook, just a short walk to the northeast from the city gates. Despite its apparent closeness to the Winterfall Village however, the mountain itself blocks a direct path and a long ride around is needed to head further south from the cave.

Moonglade Isle is an island in the middle of a lake in the Moonglade. The Horn of Cenarius was kept on it guarded by three Primal Guardians (spirits of ancient keepers of the grove and several owlbears). The night elf Sentinels led by Tyrande Whisperwind had to fight their way to through the Horde camped there, as well as three ancient guardians in order to get the horn so they could wake the sleeping druids. There were three caves, likely one for each of the spirits. Near the lake, Malfurion's barrow den was located there.

Monk abilities are abilities used by monks. Most abilities are shared between all specializations, while some are only specific to one (or two) specializations.

Prior to patch 7.0.3, a monk was always in one of the three available stances, controlling their available abilities and resource mechanics. Moonflower Valley is a fertile area located in south of Lunarfall and north of Anguish Fortress. It is home to a variety of wildlife including Pearltusk elekk, Seacliff kaliri, Shadowmoon stalkers, Moonbark ancients, and the rylak Amaukwa.
The Moonkin Festival is an event in which moonkin are trained in Moonglade.
Moonclaw Cavern is a small cave above Moonclaw Vale in Val'sharah. It is where the vile satyr Kagraxxis the Corruptor resides and oversees the corruption of Moonclaw Vale.

__NOTOC__ Moonpaw is a gray wolf serving as the mount of Thrall, after his first companion Snowsong grew too old to ride into battle. Thrall rode Moonpaw during the Horde's battle against the Widow's Bite and the Banshee loyalists at the Necropolis. Years later, Thrall and his family brought their wolves—Moonpaw, Ryala, Spring, and Winter—with them when they visited Drek'Thar in Frostwolf Keep, in Alterac Valley.
Morja is an orc quest giver located on Darkmoon Island, which is only available during the monthly Darkmoon Faire event. Morja has lost Jubjub, her frog, and only Dark Iron Ale Mug can get her back.
Moonstalker Matriarchs are saber cats found in Darkshore, usually accompanied by a Moonstalker Runt, which can make solo hunting them significantly harder than the Moonstalker Sire.

Moonshroud is created with tailoring (415); taught by trainers. Tailors who specialized in Mooncloth Tailoring previously receive 2 pieces of Moonshroud instead of one. This has been removed as of patch 4.0.1.
Moonweb Spiders are venom spiders found in southeastern Darkmoon Island.

Moonwillow Peak is a serene grove overlooking the Nightmarsh to its west in . During the Shadowmoon Valley storyline, and the Alliance Commander come to this location to drink of the Clarity Elixir. Before the oracle stone beneath the great willow, they share a vision of the Iron Horde attacking and defeating the draenei of Karabor using the power of the . By the end of the storyline, the oracle stone is no longer located beneath the willow.

Morashu is an ancient and powerful moose spirit who dwells in the Screeching Crag in Highmountain. According to Maltha Silenthoof, he has lingered in Highmountain as long as any tribe, and his presence is needed to carry out the cycle of life and death that keeps nature in balance. It is said that Morashu guides the spirits of animals when they meet their end, staying with them when the light leaves their eyes and leading them down a path where their spirits may rejoin nature. However, Morashu has recently become corrupted by two Vilewing Hexers, his antlers having become twisted into an unnatural shape. According to Maltha, this cursed state makes the moose spirit unable to guide the spirit
Moosebone Fish-Hook is a common Highmountain tauren archaeology artifact, created from 30 Highmountain Tauren Archaeology Fragments. One Highmountain Ritual-Stone may be used to solve this artifact.

The Moonwing wildkin are a group of wildkin that inhabits Silvermyst Isle on Azuremyst Isle. For many years, the wildkin were friendly to the local night elf family and lived together in harmony. When the draenei ship was crashed, pieces of its crystals spread around the area. The radiation from these crystals drove the wildlife, along with the Moonwing wildkin, mad. They attacked their former night elf friends, killing one of them and can no longer be reasoned with. Also after the Exodars fall, these owlkin began to worship Hauteur, a crazed fire elemental. Moths are flying insect beasts with powdery wings that can be found on Azeroth, Outland/, and Argus. Blue Moths are delicate denizens of Azuremyst Isle who are rumored to have healing abilities. A product of exposure to wild magical energies, the Red Moth is the unexpectedly colorful result of Azerothian moth species being released into the eco-domes of the Netherstorm. Jinyu assassins employ the Ashwing Moth as both a portable decoy and a light source to reveal weak spots in their enemy's armor. The curious Skywisp Moth is sometimes found interrupting the spells of a wandering mage or warlock.

They are mostly found in Khaz Modan, but can also be found in other dwarven territories such as Dun Garok in Hillsbrad Foothills and Dun Baldar in Alterac Valley. Some are armed with rifles acting as riflemen along with their usual axes or warhammers. Most mountaineers wear green uniforms, but a few have been spotted wearing a purple or yellow uniform. Mountain Gronn are lesser gronn found in western Nagrand. Until recently, they were in control of the ogres that inhabited the area, but when Cho'war the Pillager united the ogre clans into the Warmaul clan, he drove them out of their mountain home and named himself king. As a result, mountain gronn will attack Warmaul ogres wherever they find them, and are able to kill them with ease.

Mount Hyjal is a region of Cataclysm, and a mountain located in Northern Kalimdor. Hyjal is under heavy siege by Ragnaros, who is trying to destroy the World Tree located in the mountain's summit, Nordrassil. Malfurion Stormrage is returning from the Emerald Dream, and commands the armies of Cenarius, known as the Guardians of Hyjal. The zone makes extensive use of the terrain phasing technology.

.]] Mount Neverest is the highest mountain in all of Azeroth. Located in northwest Kun-Lai Summit, the mountain is bordered by the Shado-Li Basin to the southwest, the Shado-Pan Monastery to the northwest, the unnamed mountain pass to the north and east with the Neverest Basecamp halfway between One Keg and the monastery, and the Burlap Trail to the south. From the Neverest Basecamp, the Seeker's Folly begins, passing by endless falling snowballs and vortexes to reach Seeker's Point. From there, the path continues, unnamed, up to Neverest Pinnacle.

__NOTOC__ Mountaineer Stonegrind is a dwarven mountaineer sent to help the gnomes take down Razlo Crushcog in Dun Morogh. He commands a group of mountaineers and is recognized as a veteran who knows Dun Morogh well. He assists Gelbin Mekkatorque in defeating Razlo Crushcog.
Mountaineer Deich is a dwarven mountaineer located at Nesingwary's Retreat in Highmountain.

Mr. Pinchy is a very rare catch from high level Outland fishing spots (Highland Mixed Schools) which can only be found in three of the lakes in Terokkar Forest, all three of which require a flying mount (or druid flight form) to reach. The first two lakes are respectively above each of the faction towns in the area and completely empty of any hostile NPCs, making them pretty easy to fish; Lake Jorune above Stonebreaker Hold for Horde, and Lake Ere'Noru above Allerian Stronghold for Alliance. The third, Blackwind Lake is much larger, provides many more Highland Mixed School spawn points, and is surrounded by the dangerous denizens of Skettis within the Skethyll Mountains. For years, the good folks at Murloco's Tacos have been serving quality Murloc dishes made from only the freshest ingredients. Nakodu is a Broken Lower City faction vendor located at the Lower City market in Shattrath City.

Nahom is a small temple southeast of Ramkahen in Uldum. Sun Prophet Tumet and the Nahom Sun Priests watch over this temple and the Tombs of the Precursors usually with little defenses. As the order is given to assault Neferset City to the west, a regiment of Ramkahen soldiers were sent here to help protect it for when the Neferset attack from the east. This regiment, which Salhet was apart of, was ambushed on the way here and their captain killed, leaving Salhet in command. There is an old story about Nahom. Namuria Gladesong was the founder of the Unseen Path after the War of the Ancients. After the war, Namuria, Emmarel and their fellow night elf hunters left Mount Hyjal and returned to Highmountain and the Broken Isles. Namuria and her order sought to specifically guard against the Legion's eventual return, notably befriending Huln's daughter Arien Highmountain and joining forces with the local Highmountain tauren as she led them to Trueshot Lodge. Emmarel Shadewarden served as her eyes and ears when she had duties elsewhere. Nalmus Highmountain was a chieftain of the Highmountain Tribe and wielder of Talonclaw who lived several generations after the War of the Ancients. When word came that a mysterious beast was stalking the wilds of Stormheim, Nalmus took up Talonclaw and set out to tame or destroy the creature. He was sent off with a great feast, and the epic "Song of Talonclaw" was sung to bring him success in his quest. All felt sure he would restore peace and calm to the land. However, weeks passed without any word of Nalmus. Naga Distillers are located in the Steamvault. They are used by Warlord Kalithresh to empower himself and can be destroyed. Non-interactive versions are also found throughout Coilskar Point in Shadowmoon Valley

Narkk is a goblin located in Booty Bay in the Cape of Stranglethorn where he runs Nautical Needs. As well as selling parrots and pirate gear, he provides an Oversized Pirate Hat for Looks Like a Tauren Pirate to Me and Narkk's Handbombs for Prepare for Takeoff. During Mathias Shaw and Flynn Fairwind's visit to Booty Bay after the Fourth War, Flynn initially thought that Narkk was one of Shaw's contacts, but it turned out that the goblin is only a simple vendor. Before leaving, Flynn bought a parrot from Narkk that he named Mathias.

This unnamed river is one of the longest in the Eastern Kingdoms. It rises in the southern peaks of the Redridge Mountains, and can be seen tumbling down a waterfall in southwestern Redridge. It then flows west, bordering Duskwood and Elwynn Forest, making it the natural border between the two regions. A tributary flowing from the mountains southwest of Stormwind City tumbles into the river and there it sharply turns and heads south, marking the borderline of Westfall with Elwynn Forest, and further south, the main river continues, making the border with Duskwood. Naxt Victim is an exploration achievement earned from killing the 6 bosses summoned by the Sentinax flying around the Broken Shore. To gain access to the bosses, normal, uncommon beacons (e.g. Sentinax Beacon of Torment) must be used while under the Sentinax and the mobs summoned must be killed until they drop empowered beacons (e.g. Sentinax Beacon of Greater Torment). Continue to kill the empowered mobs until a portal stone drops (e.g. Portal-Stone: Illisthyndria), at which point the boss may be summoned and is ready to be tackled by adventurers in the area.

Neevil is a legendary goblin inventor. However he seems to be more famous for the number of devices attributed to him, many of which he denies having ever invented. He denies having any interest in techno-magical combinations, devices that combine magic and technology. Yet it seems all the devices claimed to be his, all are techno-magical in nature. Neevil' bombs" are an example of a weapon Neevil denies having invented.

Another item supposedly invented by Neevil, this device is more likely a knock-off of the original design enhanced by magic. The item resembles a standard gyroparasol, but is made of higher quality materials and has a special, malleable hand-grip that adjusts to fit its owner's fingers. If used in an area with light or no winds, it can fly or levitate. For full flight, the winds must be moderate or less.

Nemesis: Draenei Destroyer is a Buildings achievement for completing the quest Nemesis: Draenei Destroyer (quest) and grants the title Draenei Destroyer. A Level 2 Gladiator's Sanctum building is required to access the Nemesis quests.

.]] Necrorays are flying beasts native to Maldraxxus, especially the areas of Glutharn's Decay and the Sepulcher of Knowledge. They prefer to congregate around the realm's enormous decaying mushrooms and lay their eggs in small clusters within the frills of decaying fungi. When a necroray hatches, spores fly everywhere. Schnottz Excavators built several camps around the area and ended up destroying more relics than looting them from this ancient site. Myzerian oversaw the operation to prevent more failures.

Ogudei was the mogu ruler that built an edifice within the mountains of Krasarang Wilds. The Reliquary has taken interest in him, though little is known about him. Ohn'ahra is the Wild God of the Wind. She takes the form of a giant eagle spirit and has power over wind magic. She is the namesake of the Ohn'ahran Plains on the Dragon Isles, and the ancestor of all ohuna. The Maruuk centaur worship her, and the mystics of Clan Ohn'ir interpret her winds to advise their people. She also has close ties to the tauren of Highmountain and the famous spear :Talonclaw.

These immense mountains of flesh, physical manifestations of the Void, grow like cancers within the worlds of the Great Dark Beyond. Four Old Gods — Y'Shaarj, C'Thun, Yogg-Saron and N'Zoth — ruled the planet of Azeroth during its primordial age, forming what would become known as the Black Empire. Old Town is Stormwind City's oldest section, and many parts of it still predate the reconstruction of the city after its razing by the orcs during the events of the First War. As the district had not been badly ravaged, it had never needed true rebuilding. Consequently, less attention had been paid to its upkeep since then, and so while preserved, it was not nearly as pristine as the rest of the capital. It is a rustic, down-trodden place, where the streets are described as far dirtier and smellier than the other districts. Old Nefu is an elderly Highmountain tauren found inside a hut in Snowmane Village in Highmountain. He needs to be told to evacuate during Evacuate Snowmane, but stubbornly refuses to leave his home to the drogbar. This proves to be Nefu's undoing, as his lifeless body is later found next to the Understone Breach, which is created when Dargrul uses the Hammer of Khaz'goroth to destroy Snowmane. After his death, a memorial note for Nefu can be found at a shrine in Snowblind Mesa.

Onslaught Harbor is the base of operations for the Scarlet Onslaught in Icecrown within Northrend. The area is a complex of islands that the Onslaught took over off the west coast of the glacier. According to Lord-Commander Arete of the Knights of the Ebon Blade, only the battle-hardened Scarlet Crusaders who survived the Forsaken attack on New Hearthglen reside here. The Oracle Glade is the place where Malfurion Stormrage meditates. The Bloodfeather harpies have recently moved into the Glade, and a foul blight has corrupted the matron of the Teldrassil spiders, Lady Sathrah, who can sometimes be found in the far corners of the glade.

Pandarian champions are special rare mobs found wandering the continent of Pandaria. Attackable by both Alliance and Horde players, champions provide a tougher challenge than most, and drop special loot. Defeating Pandarian champions is the objective of the achievements A Worthy Opponent, Could We Find More Like That? and Glorious!. There are 56 Pandarian champions in total. Although not elites, champions have far more health than normal mobs. Paragons of Power are remnants from the ancient Gurubashi Empire. It was the only place in the Eastern Kingdoms where druid trainers resided. The night elves created a Moonwell in the center of the park square. Power over Poison teaches the young Druid the techniques needed to gain power over poison: the ability to Cure Poison. Power Word: Barrier is a Discipline priest talent. It is a Power Word ability that summons a barrier area on the ground, and all friendly players standing inside that area get a damage reduction effect. It is an exclusive choice node with Luminous Barrier.
Power of the Blue Flight are player-controlable drakes of the blue dragonflight used against Kil'jaeden in Sunwell Plateau.

Power Geode is a buff gained upon killing one of the neutral Power Geode mobs found in Molten Quarry, Ashran. The buff does not stack, but does stack with other effects such as that of the Ancient Artifact. For more information, see Molten Quarry#Power Geodes.

Praak Island is a large island somewhere off the western coast of the Howling Fjord, separated from the mainland by Lyquokk Strait. The tuskarr have typically not sailed through the strait due to the sea monster that inhabited it, instead taking the longer way around the island.

Prismatic Cloak is a Mage talent in the Arcane tree that reduces all damage taken by 2% per rank, up to 6% at max rank. This talent applies to all damage, magic and physical, making it a nice survivability talent. Its most notable effect however is the effect it has on Invisibility, turning the spell instant at maximum rank which is a massive increase to Arcane survivability in PvP settings. For this, it is considered a required talent in any serious Arcane PvP build.

A priority based rotation is a system that players use to maximize their DPS based on the worth of their abilities. The worth of a spell or ability is commonly associated with its Average Damage Per Cast Time (aDPCT). With Cataclysm and the recent changes associated with Patch_4.0.1, most players are relearning their classes and how best to put to use their new or reworked abilities. The goal is to learn how to calculate the average damage per cast time (aDPCT) of our spells and put together a priority-based rotation, not only helping our understanding and appreciation of the design process, but also (and perhaps most importantly) maximizing our DPS.

Prisoners of Jin'Zil are night elves held in cages by Witch Doctor Jin'Zil in a cave at Malaka'jin in the Stonetalon Mountains. Upon completion of Jin'Zil's Forest Magic, Jin'Zil feeds the prisoners with a poison that kills them instantly, after which their wisps can be seen flying out of the cave.

Pterrordax (sometimes pluralized as pterrordaxes), also known as pteradons, skyscreamers, or pterrorwings, are carnivorous, flying dinosaurs found on the Lost Isles, in Nazmir, Un'Goro Crater, Vol'dun, and Zuldazar. An adult pterrordax's sonic screeches are capable of turning a humanoid's eardrums to bloody pulps. Zandalari trolls are known to use pterrordaxes as flying mounts. Pterrordax eggs are incubated underneath the fossils of their forebears, allowing the hatchlings to absorb their ancestors' ferocity and intelligence. Pterrordaxes eat direhorns. Pulsing Rot-hive is an anima power obtained from anima caches in Torghast, Tower of the Damned. This power spawns Decayfly Hatchlings.

The risen are skeletal guardians created from the bones and corpses of dead warriors. Unlike a typical skeletal soldier, risen are exceptionally tough and resistant to damage.
